reason: Wrapping the connected well line in insulation seems directly useful for sheltering it from the cold.
expectation: I expect the quilt stock to insulate the water line, though it may need additional protection.

alternatives.reason: The bricks could form the protective shell, but insulating the line seems like a direct first step toward the goal.

effect: The quilt stock insulated the water line, and the shovel is now compatible with it.
reaction: That was straightforward; I’m curious how the line will be sheltered further.
reason: Using the shovel with the insulated line suggests burying it for additional protection, which fits the current goal.
expectation: I expect to bury or cover the insulated water line, though I’m unsure exactly how the shovel will be used.

alternatives.reason: The bricks could start the cabin shell, but the water line is the current goal.

effect: The trench shelters the insulated line while keeping its connections accessible; the heat tracing still needs power. The next goal is to protect the cabin without loading its skin.
reaction: The accessible connections and unpowered heat tracing make the trench feel like a practical but incomplete thermal solution.
reason: Placing the fired bricks at the cabin perimeter is the only available combination and seems suited to building the protective shell.
expectation: I expect to begin a freestanding brick wall around the cabin, though I don't know how much of the shell this will complete.

effect: The freestanding wall provides its own footing, so packed material can shelter the cabin without loading its pressure shell.
reaction: The separate footing makes the purpose of the wall clear.
reason: Using the shovel with the wall is the only available combination and suggests packing local material against it.
expectation: I expect to add local material against the wall to improve the cabin’s protection, though I’m unsure whether that completes the goal.

effect: The bermed wall completed the cabin protection goal, and the heater cycling off suggests the shelter is reducing heat loss.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the heater respond while the window still has its view.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the freestanding wall was most worthwhile because its separate footing explained how local material could shelter the cabin without loading the pressure shell.

leastWorthwhile.text: Insulating the line was a fairly plain combination on its own, with little explanation until the trench was made.

surprise.text: The trench keeps the hose connections accessible, but its heat tracing still needs power; insulation and covering alone are not presented as a complete solution.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary. The shovel and wall combinations had clear purposes, though they were the only available combinations at those points.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the expedition handles the remaining power need and what happens as the crops grow.
